messages:
maya.presales: Prospect (MediCore) asked for a compact SIG answer about encryption/KMS: want statements on at-rest/in-transit, BYOK differences across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, HSM import support, who does rotation, and a POC duration estimate. Need copy we can drop into their questionnaire.

leo.security: Paste-ready bullets: 
- In-transit: All traffic between clients and our control/data planes is protected with TLS 1.2+, TLS 1.3 recommended.
- At-rest: Persisted artifacts and customer data are encrypted with AES-256 using envelope encryption; each tenant has a unique DEK.

devin.eng: BYOK & deployment differences: 
- Hosted: Default uses Redwood-managed keys; customers can request BYOK via supported cloud KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure) using grant-based access so customers retain key control.
- Dedicated: Tenant-scoped CMKs in the customer's cloud account are supported.
- Private/on-prem: Direct integration with customer KMS or PKCS#11 HSM is supported; key material can be configured non-exportable.

leo.security: HSM & import note: We integrate with PKCS#11 HSMs and cloud HSMs. For imports where provider supports HSM-wrapped keys, Redwood supports common import patterns; if keys are non-exportable, rotation must be handled on the HSM side.

devin.eng: Rotation responsibilities: 
- Service-managed keys: Redwood rotates service/intermediate keys on our schedule and maintains key versioning.
- Customer-managed keys: Customer controls root/CMK rotation. Redwood will rewrap DEKs and migrate ciphertext on customer request or via an agreed automation.
- HSM non-exportable keys: Rotation occurs inside the HSM and is performed by the customer/ops team; Redwood assists with rewrap once new key is available.

leo.security: Plaintext handling: Redwood does not persist plaintext to disk. Transient in-memory plaintext buffers are used during active inference; we clear buffers and avoid writing unencrypted payloads to storage.

devin.eng: POC estimate (short): Typical Private HSM integration POC = ~2 weeks given network allowlists, PKCS#11 endpoint or KMS ARNs, and credentials available at kickoff. Add time for physical HSM delivery/setup if needed.

paul.sales: This is perfect. I'll paste into the SIG and send to MedCore. Can someone attach a short SOW paragraph we can send if they ask for pricing?

devin.eng: SOW blurb: "Redwood will run a targeted Private HSM integration POC to validate PKCS#11 connectivity or cloud KMS reference, exercise encryption/decryption flows and DEK rewraps, and deliver a connectivity checklist, runbook, and test logs. Estimated effort: 2 weeks with provided access; extended if physical HSM setup required."

sig-helper-bot: :white_check_mark: SIG section "Encryption & KMS" updated by leo.security and devin.eng.

maya.presales: Thanks team 1 I'll send this out and open a follow-up thread if they request pricing.
